record_identity.title: More than 100 Baidu Apollo Go robotaxis stopped in live Wuhan traffic during a system failure

incident_identity.historical_event_name: 31 March 2026 Apollo Go Wuhan fleet outage
incident_identity.date_basis: Wuhan traffic police reported that calls began at approximately 20:57 on 31 March 2026; Reuters and AIID record the same occurrence.

summary: A reported system failure caused more than 100 Baidu Apollo Go robotaxis in Wuhan to stop in live traffic, including on elevated roads, stranding passengers until police and company personnel responded. Authorities reported that passengers exited safely and no injuries were recorded. The technical root cause remains under investigation in the public record.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Reuters reports Wuhan traffic police described the event as a system failure affecting more than 100 Apollo Go vehicles. AIID Incident 1460 preserves the same occurrence and affected-system entities. Public evidence establishes correlated fleet-wide stoppage and passenger stranding but not the specific failing component.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence demonstrates a material correlated-failure mode in embodied autonomous infrastructure: a shared system failure can simultaneously immobilise a large fleet in live road environments. Without a confirmed root cause, VIGIL does not infer whether the mechanism involved central control, communications, cloud infrastructure, fleet orchestration or vehicle-local software.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: A shared failure can immobilise many autonomous vehicles at once, turning a component or fleet dependency into a city-scale operational disruption. Embodied systems therefore need continuity, fail-safe behaviour and correlated-dependency controls that are assessed at fleet level as well as vehicle level.
assessment_boundaries: The specific technical root cause and failing component are not established in the reviewed public evidence.
The evidence does not establish whether the vehicles departed from a particular designed fallback state because the relevant design requirement is not public.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Current-taxonomy review against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.6 retains the occurrence as unclassified. The evidence establishes correlated immobilisation of more than 100 Apollo Go robotaxis in live Wuhan traffic, but the responsible technical or governance mechanism remains unknown. VIGIL-FC-000037 Control Availability Ambiguity was tested but no specific governance control required for a material decision is shown to have had an uncertain callable or coverage state. VIGIL-FC-000040 Control-State Preservation Failure is not established because no already-operative governance control state is shown to have been lost or weakened across a transition. VIGIL-FC-000070 Safe-Exit Persistence Failure is not established because the vehicles stopped rather than continuing objective pursuit after an invalid continuation state. Fleet-scale correlation and operational severity do not by themselves identify a selectable governance mechanism.

classification_review_provenance.method: deterministic current-taxonomy re-adjudication using preserved Incident evidence and complete VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.6 class-set review
classification_review_provenance.reviewer: OpenAI ChatGPT / GPT-5.6 Sol under human-directed VIGIL governance
classification_review_provenance.authority_boundary: Taxonomy version reviewed: 0.6.6 (beta; publication date 2026-09-21). Candidate classes tested: VIGIL-FC-000037, VIGIL-FC-000040, VIGIL-FC-000070. Accepted mappings: none. Rejected or not independently established: VIGIL-FC-000037: no required governance control with materially ambiguous availability is established; VIGIL-FC-000040: no operative control state is shown to have been lost across a transition; VIGIL-FC-000070: the evidence shows fleet stoppage, not persistence after a warranted safe exit. External-assessment material was checked where present or materially attributable in preserved sources; no external assessment was treated as automatic taxonomy evidence. Review used preserved canonical Incident evidence only and performed no new external research. Retained unclassified under taxonomy 0.6.6; the common-mode fleet failure is established, but its responsible mechanism is not.
